title: The Last Summit
premise: Beatrix Villalobos, a disgraced mountain guide blacklisted after a client's death she may or may not have caused, is hired by a desperate widow to find an expedition that vanished while seeking the source of the Río Blanco — a river whose headwaters lie inside a protected reserve closed after a mining massacre the government erased from record. Following the river upstream with the widow's son, Elias, Beatrix discovers the missing expedition was actually hunting evidence of the massacre, guarded by survivors turned wardens who remember everything the world was paid to forget. At the frozen cirque called the Last Summit, Beatrix must choose between destroying the evidence to save the hostages the wardens have taken, or letting people die so the truth survives; she finds a third way, broadcasting the testimony from the peak itself. The novel ends with the river's source exposed to the world, Beatrix's name cleared but her guide's license voluntarily surrendered, and she and Elias walking back downstream toward a justice that will now be slow, legal, and real.
about_author: Juniper Brightwater is the pen name of a former river guide who spent a decade leading expeditions through South American headwaters before turning to writing full-time. She lives in a converted boathouse with too many maps and a dog named Compass.

chapters.title: Blacklist
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. In a border-town cantina, Beatrix drinks off another rejected permit and counts her debts, until a widow named Inés Solano offers her a fortune to find the expedition her husband led up the Río Blanco — an expedition the government insists never existed. Beat: humiliation meeting a last chance.

chapters.title: The Widow's Son
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Beatrix provisions the journey and meets Elias, Inés's estranged son, who blames his father's obsession for his mother's ruin and intends to drag the expedition home by force. Their first clash on the trail establishes the love-versus-duty fault line. Beat: reluctant alliance.

chapters.title: Dead Air
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Following the last radio coordinates, they find the expedition's abandoned basecamp: tents slashed, radios smashed, and a journal page describing 'voices in the canyon that know our names.' Beat: dread — the mystery turns from disappearance to warning.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias narrates a night crossing and a near-drowning, during which Beatrix saves him and finally admits the truth of the client's death that blacklisted her — she chose the summit over the storm warning. Beat: vulnerability; Elias begins to see her clearly.

chapters.title: The Wardens
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. They are captured by the wardens — survivors of the San Rafael mining massacre who became the reserve's secret guardians. Their leader, an old woman named Doña Rufina, reveals the missing expedition came hunting massacre evidence and is being held at the source. Beat: the moral ground shifts.

chapters.title: Testimony in Ice
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Shown the wardens' archive — photographs, a miner's ledger, recorded names hidden in a glacier cave — Elias realizes his father came not for glory but to carry the truth out, and that Inés knew. Beat: betrayal and reckoning with inherited duty.

chapters.title: Terms of the Mountain
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. The wardens offer a trade: the hostages for the evidence, which must never leave the mountain. Beatrix, who once chose a summit over people, must now decide whether truth is worth lives — and whether she's the person to make that call. Beat: the novel's moral hinge.

chapters.title: Ascent
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV, interwoven with Elias's. A storm-battered night climb to the Last Summit, Beatrix leading hostages, wardens, and Elias up the route that ruined her, using every skill her disgrace taught her. Beat: redemption in motion; the past and present converge on the ice.

chapters.title: The Last Summit
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. At the peak, with a dying satellite transmitter salvaged from basecamp, Beatrix broadcasts the massacre testimony live as the wardens stand down and the hostages descend — the third way between silence and sacrifice. Beat: climax; love and duty reconciled in a single act.

chapters.title: Downriver
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Weeks later, hearings begin in the capital; the evidence is safe, Inés and Elias reconcile over his father's true legacy, and Beatrix, cleared but changed, mails back her reinstated license and asks Elias where the river goes next. Beat: resolution — justice begins, and so does love.
